lines: a16z's Martin Casado argues AI has turned software from an engineering-constrained problem into a capital-constrained one, so money can now convert directly into technical output and the 'Mythical Man Month' limit largely falls away.

He says investors must know whether they are acting as productive, traditional finance, frontier or speculative investors, because applying the wrong framework gets disruptive technology rejected on lagging metrics.

He puts the competitive lifespan of a state-of-the-art model at just three to six months, forcing perpetual iteration, and contends that in fast-growing markets the focus on moats is often a distraction from growth velocity.

Casado prefers judging network effects by their mathematical shape (superlinear, linear or sublinear) and says strategic M&A rests on personal trust between founders and buyers, not poker-style auctions and leaks.
He calls the chase for 'non-consensus' deals an ego-driven fallacy in efficient private markets, and argues more capital deployment expands the market rather than playing a zero-sum game.
podcast: Invest Like the Best with Patrick O'Shaughnessy
title: Martin Casado on Frontier Model Economics, AI's Slowdown, and the Cursor Deal - [Invest Like the Best, EP.498]
